subject.title: browser tool: include current page URL in before_tool_call params for act/type actions

question: Should OpenClaw expose the current browser tab URL to `before_tool_call` handlers for browser `act`/`type`, and should that be param enrichment or a supported hook-time query/context helper?
rationale: This changes a security-sensitive plugin API and URL exposure boundary; automation can implement the chosen contract, but should not decide URL leakage, redaction, and compatibility semantics.

options.title: Add Hook-Time URL Contract
options.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL before browser `act`/`type` hooks decide whether to rewrite, approve, or block the call.

options.title: Add Query Helper
options.body: Keep hook params unchanged and provide a supported hook context/helper that plugins can call to resolve the active browser URL at decision time.

options.title: Keep Plugin Workarounds
options.body: Leave URL caching and fail-secure cold-cache blocking to credential plugins, accepting duplicated ecosystem complexity.

recommendation.title: Add Hook-Time URL Contract
recommendation.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL before browser `act`/`type` hooks decide whether to rewrite, approve, or block the call.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans browser tool routing and browser URL policy, and steipete is the strongest current history signal on those files.
